THE HONEST LIMIT OF THIS ROW'S HEADLINE, added at s0012 close after ajcr-charts pointed out on
I-0494 that a reduction owes TWO probes and I had run only one on my own. 'The eps-half is OPEN,
not false' is a claim about the NO-GO: forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling does not bear on a
hypothesis naming no adaptation. IT IS SILENT ABOUT SATISFIABILITY. The mirror risk is real and
UNMEASURED: if the window quotient at the universal point can never be projective of constant
rank g, then the eps-half has been reduced to a FALSE hypothesis -- which passes every sorry
census and every axiom probe, because it is then a theorem.

Note the asymmetry with the junk probe that refuted DAT-J's Abel square: that residue was vacuous
because its witness was CONSUMER-CHOSEN. Here the window quotient is determined by d, so vacuity
is impossible and satisfiability is the only live failure mode. The 'not silently stronger' probe
IS discharged (divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified_of_quotientData recovers the landed
chart-typed statement as a corollary); the satisfiability probe is owed and is the cheapest next
measurement on this row.

SUPERSEDING THE SATISFIABILITY CAVEAT ABOVE -- I RAN THE PROBE AND THE EPS-HALF IS DISCHARGED, NOT
MERELY OPEN (s0012 close, commit 32476f85a, root build 9280 jobs EXIT=0, divFamEps_eq_of_le
axiom-clean vs a control that fires sorryAx).

  divFamEps_eq_of_le (Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivQuot.lean)
    the eps-pair identity at an ARBITRARY F : DivFam C R pi g from THE TWO CONTAINMENTS ALONE --
    no projectivity hypothesis, no rank hypothesis, no certificate.

WHY: Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean ALREADY carries DivFam.projective_window_quotient (:106) and
DivFam.rankAtStalk_window_quotient (:117) for EVERY F at EVERY window a >= windowM_choice,

THE SHARP READING, and it retracts this row's own framing across five sessions: THE EPS-HALF OF U2
WAS NEVER GATED ON A CERTIFICATE AT ALL -- not on the original (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified

The eps layer never asked for one beyond that.

SO THE PARTITION IS NOT 'eps open, class refuted'. It is: eps DISCHARGED, and 100% of U2's
remaining content is PRODUCING THE CLASS over the chart ring -- exactly the face protection I-0492's
widening exists to supply, and cert-r2's divFamZarAff_of_swallowing_affineOpen is the live
candidate. The straddling probe now decides that and nothing else.

METHOD NOTE, worth more than the result: this came from running the probe ajcr-charts named on
I-0494 -- a reduction owes BOTH 'not vacuous' and 'not silently stronger'. My hypothesis was
DETERMINED by the data rather than consumer-chosen, so the live risk was UNSATISFIABILITY rather
than vacuity; checking it turned a caveat into a theorem and refuted my own headline of an hour
earlier.

ANNOUNCES THAT THE WIDENED THETA-LAYER LETS cert-r2's PRODUCER REACH U2. THAT IS FALSE, AND THE

  AffAdaptation.isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling
    if ONE piece of a widened cover holds a point outside V0 AND a point outside V1, then
    ChartTyping C R pi D is EMPTY.

Every declaration in Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean is indexed by a ChartTyping. cert-r2's
producer runs through a cover whose support sits inside ONE piece W, and the straddling hypotheses
of forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling say the support has a point outside V0 and one outside V1 --
both then in W. So ON EXACTLY THE DIVISORS I-0492's WIDENING EXISTS FOR, the index is uninhabited
and every theorem in the new module is vacuous. Compounding it: the tree's ONLY ChartTyping producer
is FinCoverData.toChartTyping, the migration FROM the chart-typed carrier, so every instantiation
available today factors through FinCoverData.

MY ERROR, and it is the reusable part: I-0492 clause 3 keeps ChartTyping separate from the
certificate clauses so a certificate never REQUIRES a chart typing -- a statement about what is
PERMITTED. I read it as evidence about what is INHABITED. Only the second question decides whether a
layer indexed by that datum is usable. Recorded shape: isolating-a-residue-as-a-class. CHECK
INHABITATION OF AN INDEX BEFORE PRICING ANYTHING STATED OVER IT.

Found by a fresh-context review (I-0779/I-0782); re-proved independently before accepting.

follows from thetaEval_mem in the same file. Over-priced in the same session I under-priced
inhabitation.

THE LIVE QUESTION THIS LEAVES, for whoever picks the row up: a chart-free route to the eps-value,
or a producer of a ChartTyping-free Theta layer. The straddling probe is NOT what decides it.

SO THE PARTITION NEEDS A THIRD ROW:
  eps-value at a DivFam        DISCHARGED (s0012).
  eps-value at a DivFamZarAff  was UNSTATEABLE -- no Theta-layer existed.
  the class over the chart ring PRODUCED by cert-r2, in the wrong carrier.
DivisorFamilyAffFraming is right that the eps STATEMENT is carrier-indifferent; the eps FACTS
are not, and nobody had separated statement from facts.

LANDED THIS SESSION (Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean, commits d2e47343f 358ed7257 94d526b0e
d05c316b0 91f702164; sorry-free, rooted, kernel EXIT=0 zero diagnostics, axiom-clean vs a

  AffAdaptation.thetaEval / thetaGluedEval / thetaEval_mem / germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal

  the (c2) substrate: gluedSubalgebra, unitGluedSubmodule (+_one, +_thetaOvlUnit by rfl),
    mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule, unitGluedOver, thetaSpan/thetaInvSpan,
    thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one, IsThetaPaired, isThetaPaired_of_one_mem
  the sections: relFiberCoordSidePow, thetaSectionSide

WHY ker_thetaGluedEval IS THE FACE: its RHS is LITERALLY the same term as the chart-typed
DivisorAdaptation.ker_thetaGluedEval (DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:350) -- the vanishing submodule
names d and the two pinned charts and NO cover. So divisorWindow, its comap, is the same
submodule on both carriers, and a widened windowQuotEquiv has its left-exactness half.

IT WAS A PORT, NOT MATHEMATICS: the Theta layer's chart-dependence is one Bool per piece, and
the side-uniform API already existed and is used by ~60 files (relThetaResSide,
relThetaSideUnit, relThetaResSide_matching, DivSchemeFamilySide.lean:155/:180/:194), needing
only piece <= relPinnedChart (side j) -- verbatim ChartTyping.piece_le
(DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:204), the datum I-0492 clause 3 kept SEPARATE from the certificate
so exactly this could happen.

TWO MEASUREMENTS, NEITHER PREDICTED:
 * THE PORT IS SHORTER THAN THE ORIGINAL. Chart-typed thetaEval_mem runs a four-case rcases on
   the Sum index with two hand-built containments and a Units.inv_mul step; widened it is ONE
   relThetaResSide_matching. The whole (c2) substrate elaborated clean on the FIRST pass.
 * THE JOINT COVER ADDS ONE REAL STEP. Chart-typed, a point of V0 is always covered by a
   chart-0 piece; jointly the piece containing z may be assigned to the OTHER chart, so the two
   sides must be compared through the matching unit. Genuine content -- and the template already
   existed: ThetaGeneratorSeed.le_vanishingSubmodule (DivSchemeFamily.lean:397) does exactly
   this on D.piece z inf relPinnedChart b with the side from a Bool.

A SAME-SESSION SELF-CORRECTION: the (c2) commit claimed the pinned charts enter that route at
EXACTLY ONE place (isThetaPaired_of_sectionWitness). Imprecise, retracted: thetaSectionFst/Snd's
Sum-match only decides which side's coordinate to use, the same Bool, so the sections port too.

WHAT IS GENUINELY STILL OWED ON THIS ROUTE, three items:
 1. thetaSectionSide_mem -- the widened membership. This is the four-case cocycle argument
    (thetaSectionFst_mem, DivisorFamilyThetaSections.lean:321): each case a different identity
    (1, the cocycle, its inverse, 1), the inr/inl case needing a resHom_relFiberCoordPow rewrite

 2. the widened IsThetaPaired, from 1 via a widened isThetaPaired_of_sectionWitness.
 3. the widened finite/projective/rankAtStalk_thetaGlued (mechanical from 2 --
    InvertibleModuleTransfer is carrier-generic), hence a widened windowQuotEquiv and the
    eps-value over the widened carrier.

NOT silently stronger (thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one is the automatic half, so the content is
exactly the reverse inclusion, as chart-typed). Whether it is SATISFIABLE over a widened cover is
open, and it is item 1. Recording the limit rather than leaving it for a reviewer.

STANDING AND STILL BINDING:
 * U2 IS NOT PROVED AND NO GATE HAS CLEARED. Nothing produces an IsChartClause, and the widened

 * The endpoint still carries hO, hchi and the ambient curve instances.

Full write-up: informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md section 7.13.


APPENDED AT s0014 CLOSE -- THE PROBE I SAID I OWED, RUN, AND IT COMES BACK POSITIVE (commit
932f7ea38, kernel EXIT=0, axiom-clean vs a control reporting sorryAx).

  AffAdaptation.isThetaPaired_zero : IsThetaPaired A tau 0

holds for EVERY widened cover, adaptation and chart typing: at a = 0 the theta cocycle is 1
(relThetaCocycle_zero), so every thetaOvlUnit is 1 (new side-uniform relThetaSideUnit_zero /
thetaOvlUnit_zero -- the Bool form of FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero), both spans are the
equalizer algebra itself, and the pairing is unconditional.

SO THE WIDENED IsThetaPaired IS SATISFIABLE, and the residue at a > 0 is genuinely OPEN rather
than a reduction to a false hypothesis. That closes the second of the two probes this row owed;
the first (not silently stronger) was already discharged by thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one.

WHAT THE PROBE DOES NOT SHOW: nothing about a > 0. The content there is item 1 above -- the
manufactured sections' membership, a genuine four-case cocycle argument. The probe separates
'open' from 'false'; it does not shrink the obligation.

FINAL APPEND, s0014 close. A FRESH-CONTEXT REVIEW (I-0769) FOUND THE FACE WAS NAMED AND NOT
PLUGGED IN, and it is now plugged in (commit dd3d22fae): nothing connected
AffAdaptation.ker_thetaGluedEval to divisorWindow, because the chart-typed connection runs through
windowCarve / ker_windowCarve (DivisorFamilyWindow:158/:166) and no widened analogue existed.

  AffAdaptation.windowCarve / ker_windowCarve / windowCarve_surjective
  AffAdaptation.windowQuotEquiv  -- THE VEHICLE whose absence made the eps-value at a
                                    DivFamZarAff unstateable. Now conditional on NOTHING except
                                    surjectivity of the widened evaluation.

So item 3 of the ledger above is reduced: the widened windowQuotEquiv EXISTS, and what remains
between it and the widened eps-value is exactly widened-evaluation surjectivity (which is the
(c2) transport, i.e. items 1-2).

ALSO CORRECTED, against my own phrasing in three places: 'divisorWindow is the same submodule on
both carriers' is true and EMPTY -- divisorWindow takes only d and hH1 and never mentioned a

### 7.5 What `Challenge.lean:99` reduces to today

Composing with the frozen discharge `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`, the target is now exactly:

> **a Zariski atlas of `pic0SigmaFunctor C`** — an index `ι`, schemes `X i`, maps
> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that (1) each `f i` is a relatively
> representable open immersion, (2) `Sigma.desc f` is Zariski-locally surjective, (3) each chart's
> structure morphism is locally of finite type and the glued object is quasi-compact.

Sheafhood, the 01JJ gluing, the Σ-descent and both finiteness certificates are discharged.

**Three corrections a ground review forced on the first draft of this subsection, all of which
matter to anyone planning off it.**

* **The atlas is NOT finite, so the producer to aim at is `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace`
  (`JacobianDataCharts.lean:199`), not `ofCharts`.** The chart index is
  `ChartIndex C := (m : ℕ) × {Σ // 0 ≤ Σ ∧ deg Σ = m·d₁ − g}` (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md:161`),
  a `Σ` over all `m : ℕ`, and the worksheet says at :66-71 that the `m`-strata do not collapse, so
  no uniform bound exists. `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never needed finiteness (being locally of
  finite type is local on the source); the whole finiteness burden therefore collapses onto the
  single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued object — which is the DAT-J image argument, a
  theorem about the Jacobian and not bookkeeping.
* **Clause (2) is not a free-standing leaf; it IS the gate.** The only builder of an `f i` is
  `abelSigmaChart` (`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:203`), which consumes
  `(divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy`, and `divFunctor` is by definition the functor of *locally
  certified* families (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean:41-45`). So (2) asserts that certified
  families cover — which is exactly what the no-go denies. See §7.6.
* Only clause (3) is genuinely cheap.

Everything below the atlas — L9 through L14 — exists to produce (1) and (2).

## 7.6 The gate is L8, not U2 — and that is the round's main finding

Inbox **I-0365**. The framing "the divrep tail is independent of the certificate; the certificate
gates U2" is false, but not in the direction the tree assumed.

`DivFamZar` is **by definition** a quotient of *locally certified* families
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224` the setoid, `:235` the def, `:71` `IsLocallyCertified` — note it
localises on the base only). So certificates are **free on the consuming side**:
`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433`) is a landed theorem,
unfolded by every classifier keystone (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128/:176/:230`,
`DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361/:363`), and `IsDivRepClassify` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90`)
quantifies over certified families as a *hypothesis*, so their scarcity makes it easier, not harder.

The bite is on the other side. The no-go (`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:123` — clause (c1) *is*
leak-freeness — and `:131`) says `DivFamZar` is blind to connected divisors meeting both pinned
fibres. So `divFunctor C π g` is a **proper subfunctor** of degree-`g` relative divisors.
Representing it is not the problem; the L9–L13 tail does that honestly. The problem is that a
too-small divisor functor **cannot cover Pic⁰**: the Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally
surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses are the invisible divisors are never hit.

One nuance that sharpens where to look: the no-go's hypothesis is `IsPreconnected d.supportLocus`,
and **over a field it is vacuous** — the support of a divisor is a finite set of closed points, so
preconnected forces a single point, which cannot meet two disjoint fibres. The blindness is a
purely *relative* phenomenon: a family over a positive-dimensional base whose total support is a
connected horizontal curve sweeping from `π⁻¹(0)` to `π⁻¹(∞)` is invisible, and base shrinking does
not help because every neighbourhood of the crossing contains points on both sides. So
Riemann–Roch-level, fibrewise coverage is untouched — but local surjectivity of a *presheaf* map is
tested on arbitrary scheme tests, which is exactly the relative direction.

**Consequences.** (i) Stop calling U2 or the affine package "the gate": they are tail work and are
nearly finished. (ii) Do not attack L8 against `divFunctor` as it stands — it is arguably false,
not merely hard. (iii) Judge R1 and R2 by whether they widen `DivFamZar` enough for L8, not by
whether they make a certificate easier to prove. A third widening is worth costing beside them:
replace `IsLocallyCertified` outright by the standard relative effective Cartier divisor (finite
locally free of rank `g` over the base), which carries no chart-adaptation artifact at all.

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π] (n : ℕ)

/-- **The divisor functor** (DD-2 S6b, the pinned name): the locally certified
degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,
with the glued restriction `divFamZar.map` along arbitrary test morphisms — the
`picDegLayerFunctor` house pattern. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
  obj T := divFamZar C π n T.unop
  map g := ↾divFamZar.map C π n g.unop
  map_id T := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZar.map_id C π n s)
  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T''.unop => z.1 U)
      (divFamZar.map_comp C π n g.unop h.unop s)

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
    (divFunctor C π n).obj T = divFamZar C π n T.unop :=
  rfl

===== Zar 55-95 =====

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The locally certified pin -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **The Addendum-2 frozen pin** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): a
local-equation system on the relative curve is *locally certified* in degree `n` if
some span-⊤ family `g : Fin m → R` carries certified divisor families over the
localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` that are divisor-equal to the pulled system.
The pullback's regularity hypothesis is discharged once and for all by the Kit's
open-immersion lemma — the comparison of an away localization is an open immersion
(the S4 instance, provided by `haveI`). -/
def IsLocallyCertified (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin m,
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) π n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))

variable {C R π}

/-- **The locally certified pin respects divisor equality**: the local `DivEq`s
transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
===== Zar 215-245 =====

/-! ## The locally certified divisor-functor value -/

variable (C R π)
variable (n : ℕ)

/-- The divisor-equality setoid on locally certified systems (Addendum 2's mirror of
`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
  iseqv :=
    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

/-- **The locally certified divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`**
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)

namespace DivFamZar

variable {C R π n}

/-- The class of a locally certified system. -/
def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
    DivFamZar C R π n :=
  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/

69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩

199	/-- **The general-test classifier of the affine package**: the affine classifiers of the
200	values of `F` at the affine opens of `T.left`, glued over the locally directed cover of
201	`T.left` by its affine opens.  The gluing datum is the compatibility with the transition
202	maps `T.left.homOfLE`, which is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar`
203	(`overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar`) applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
204	noncomputable def classifyGlobal
205	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
206	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) : T ⟶ DivOver :=
207	  Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected (X := T) (Y := DivOver)
208	    T.left.directedAffineCover (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
209	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)

242	    ι_classifyGlobal hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F W, classifyPiece,

258	          (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F)

262

266	affine-open test objects, and at each of those the uniqueness theorem

269	theorem classifyGlobal_pullGlobal

271	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
272	    classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)

275	          (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v)

294	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F

300	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D f v

9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60

140	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
141	    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :

146	/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned
147	
148	With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single

161	/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction

163	
164	This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition

207	      = V.ι ≫ chartHom C (fun _ : ι => f) i := by

210	  -- the `Over.sigmaExtension` transition map precomposes the structure morphism, and
211	  -- `f`'s naturality moves the restriction across `f`.
212	  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
213	  have hnat := congrArg Sigma.fst
214	    (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f.naturality (V.ι).op) (𝟙 X))

9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59

61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/

77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109

112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;

125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

103	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
104	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,

109	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t))
110	            (Scheme.CechPic.map

160	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
161	with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.
162	
163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
164	
165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
168	  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
169	  other route may use this theorem immediately;
170	* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
171	  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
172	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
173	  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
174	  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
175	  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
176	  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
177	  well as unusable. -/
178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
183	
184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
185	
186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
192	
193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
194	
195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
200

304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,

306	
307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite

309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
312	
313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
319	*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with

321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
329	  -- other pointwise.
330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
335	  rw [hset]
336	  exact isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField hπ D

98	/-! ## The transport -/
99	
100	variable (C π) in
101	/-- **THE TRANSPORT** — `hplus` at an arbitrary extension `L` from `hfib` at `κ(t)`.
102	
103	This is the declaration `Pic0ChartPresentationConverse`'s header advertises by name and which did
104	not exist.  Under the tower compatibility `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` — the one thing that is *not*
105	automatic, and the third component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns — the plus-class
106	identity at `κ(t)` implies the same identity at `L`.
107	
108	Proof: apply `PicEtAff.map C L` to `hfib t`.  `PicEtAff.map_map` collapses the two-step
109	restriction on the left; `PicEtAff.map_unit` moves it through the unit on the right; and
110	`relCurveMap_comp` over `A → κ(t) → L` identifies the two-step pull of `D.cechPicClass` with the
111	one-step pull `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` names.  Three functoriality laws, no geometry. -/
112	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
113	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
114	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
115	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
116	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] [Algebra A L]
117	    [IsScalarTower k A L]
118	    [IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
119	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :
120	    IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L := by
121	  have h := congrArg (PicEtAff.map C L) (hfib t)
122	  rw [PicEtAff.map_map, PicEtAff.map_unit, relPicAlgMap_mk] at h
123	  refine h.trans (congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C L) (congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)) ?_))
124	  -- the two-step pull `A → κ(t) → L` is the one-step pull `A → L`.  Rewriting the RHS's
125	  -- morphism into the composite keeps the `CechPic` type index fixed, which is what makes
126	  -- this a legal `rw` where rewriting the LHS is not (the two spellings `relCurve C κ(t)`
127	  -- and `(C ⊗ overSpec k κ(t)).left` are `rfl`-equal but block the motive).
128	  rw [← relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := A)
129	      (R' := Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) (R'' := L),
130	    Scheme.CechPic.map_comp]
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-! ## The descent step with the tower restricted
134	
135	The transport above cannot be fed to `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` as it stands,
136	and the reason is a genuine finding about that theorem's statement rather than a typing nuisance.
137	Its `hplus` binder reads
138	
139	  `∀ (L) … (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L), IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L`
140	
141	— universally quantified over the `A`-algebra structure on `L`, with only the `k`-tower imposed.
142	That is **strictly stronger than the theorem consumes**: its proof obtains the `A`-structure from
143	its own `htow` argument and uses `hplus` at *that* instance only.  And the extra strength is not
144	harmless, because `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` mentions `relCurveMap C A L`, which depends on the
145	`A`-algebra structure: for an `Algebra A L` unrelated to the composite `A → κ(t) → L`, the
146	right-hand side pulls `D.cechPicClass` along a different morphism and the identity has no reason
147	to hold.  So the `∀`-form is not merely unprovable from `hfib` — it is the wrong statement, and
148	`hfib` cannot imply it.
149	
150	This is the failure mode `price-the-instances-not-the-data` names, occurring inside a binder: the
151	hypothesis quantifies instances, and quantifying one instance too freely turns a provable
152	obligation into an unprovable one.  So the step is restated below with the tower compatibility
153	`IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` in the binder — exactly the third component
154	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns and which the landed step already destructures and
155	then discards.  The proof is the landed one; only the binder changes. -/
156	
157	variable (C π) in
158	/-- **The descent step, with the `A`-tower in `hplus`'s binder** — otherwise
159	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` verbatim.
160	
161	The landed form asks for the plus-class identity at *every* `A`-algebra structure on `L`; this
162	asks for it only at those compatible with `A → κ(t) → L`, which is all its proof ever uses and
163	all that `hfib` can give (see the section note above).  With this binder the transport
164	`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` applies, and CHART-U(b)'s residue follows from `hfib`
165	alone. -/
166	theorem hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
167	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
168	    (t : (overSpec k A).left)
169	    (hplus : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
170	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
171	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
172	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L)
173	      (_ : IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L),
174	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L)
175	    (h : IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)) :
176	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
177	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLk, hLK, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
178	  obtain ⟨hAL, hAtow, hATow⟩ := towerOfResidueFieldExtension (k := k) t L
179	  have hid : PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
180	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
181	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
182	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass)) := by
183	    rw [← hM]
184	    exact hplus L hLf hLk hLK hLtow hAL hAtow hATow
185	  have hMcl : M = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass :=
186	    relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C (overSpec k L)
187	      (PicEtAff.unit_injective C L hid)
188	  refine (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
189	    (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).mpr ⟨W, ?_, hW1⟩
190	  rw [hW, hMcl]
191	
192	/-! ## CHART-U(b)'s residue from `hfib` alone -/
193	
194	variable (C π) in
195	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` FROM `hfib` ALONE** — no `hplus` side condition.
196	
197	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` asks for `hfib` *and* the per-point identity at every
198	extension.  The transport above supplies the second from the first, and
199	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` supplies the tower instance the transport needs, so the caller
200	owes only `hfib`.
201	
202	**What this settles about the CHART-U(b) row.**  The row's state as of 2026-07-29 was "both
203	halves of the pointwise presentation are witness-free, and what remains is a `cechPicClass`
204	base-change identity at every extension of `κ(t)`, strictly more than `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`
205	asks".  That gap is now closed in the *cheap* direction the row did not expect: the extra
206	strength is not extra content, because the identity at `L` is the identity at `κ(t)` pushed
207	along `PicEtAff.map`.  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self` measured the gap from below (at
208	`L := κ(t)` the two coincide by `Iff.rfl`); this measures it from above, and the two together say
209	the generalisation in `L` costs nothing.
210	
211	So `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's named residue, CHART-U(b)'s one remaining obligation, and
212	the thing `ChartLocusAffineLocal` reduces `haff` to — now rests on exactly one hypothesis:
213	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, a witness-free, `H¹`-free, divisor-free identity of plus classes at the
214	residue fields. -/
215	theorem isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
216	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
217	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :
218	    IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D := by
219	  refine isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse C π hfib fun t hsplit => ?_
220	  refine hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower C π μ D t
221	    (fun L _ _ _ _ _ _ _ => ?_) hsplit
222	  exact isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower C π μ D t L hfib
223	
224	end

226	end AlgebraicGeometry

## What this does NOT do

It produces no class over a chart ring, so it clears no gate: U2 is unproved and, per
roadmap `…divrep.u2`, the production of a chart class with the tautological ε remains the
G-4 obligation.  What changes is what a producer has to exhibit — a class whose classifier
*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
endpoint also still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances.
-/

10	
11	## What this file closes
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
15	
16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
18	
19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.
27	
28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
34	
35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
36	automatic:
37	
38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
45	
46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
53	
54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
